accepts.because: a turn on its way to one of this organisation's members, where it meets that member's screen before anything of the member's own. The level is a boundary and a namespace, not a participant: it reads nothing, decides nothing and holds nothing, so the turn arrives at the member exactly as the caller sent it, context and all. Derived from the accepts list of member@1.6.0

a question against a member's memory, from outside that member's organisation. The namespace does not know what a recall is and must not: it carries the hop and context keys the member's own door reads (hop.recall_query, hop.memory_tier, the window pair, context.audience_set, context.channel) across the boundary untouched. Derived from the accepts list of member@1.6.0

a read against a member's curated record -- who is this person, who are they to the asker, what may this audience be told. It crosses the namespace on its way in; the level is a boundary, and identity is decided one level down by that member's affinity, never here. Derived from the accepts list of member@1.6.0

a write against that same record: a correction, a trust or disclosure decision, a subscription. A namespace neither authorises nor records it -- the actor is edge truth at the member's own door, and this boundary only lets the proposal reach it. Derived from the accepts list of member@1.6.0

the builder's answer on its way back into the member it belongs to. The org reads nothing in it and answers nothing: it owns a name and a boundary, and this lane crosses it without touching it. Derived from the accepts list of member@1.6.0

a demand that one of this organisation's members hand out its memory as a versioned document. The namespace does not know what an export is and carries no key for it -- the lane's context is empty at the member and empty here. The parts never cross this boundary: they land on disk inside the member, and what crosses back out is the one word that says the set is complete. Derived from the accepts list of member@1.6.0

one part of a memory document, on its way to the hive of the member it belongs to. It is the return leg of `in_export` and crosses this boundary exactly as untouched: the level is a namespace, not a participant -- it reads no part, decides nothing about what may enter, and hands the message to `./members` for the per-member edge to place. Which member it belongs to is the mutation's edge, the same way `in_build_result` finds its generation. The receipt rides the `dump` lane the member already drains. Derived from the accepts list of member@1.6.0

the mutation receipt, GH #553: the graph moved, and the door said so. This level is a namespace and a boundary for it like for every other transit lane -- it takes no part in what the receipt means, it only carries it into `./members`, and declaring it is what makes it a mandatory hop under ADR-0020: nothing may carry this lane past a level that declares it. Derived from member@1.6.0

emits.because: what a member answered, on its way back out through the boundary: the brief its `affinity` produced, or -- since member@1.4.0 (GH #454) -- a turn ANSWERED whose caller named no channel of that member. It leaves exactly as the member produced it: a namespace does not rewrite what crosses it and does not keep a copy -- what a member knows belongs to the member (GH #122, the three-holders ruling). Derived from the emits list of member@1.6.0

the bundle a member's memory produced for an asker OUTSIDE that member, on its way back out through the boundary (GH #533). The namespace does not know what a recall is and does not know who asked: it carries the answer and the reply-to token on `hop.recall_caller` across untouched, exactly as it carries the question in on `in_recall`. Without the lane, the answer to a question this level itself let through would die HERE as no_route -- the defect GH #533 took out of the member, rebuilt one level up. Derived from the emits list of member@1.6.0

a proposed change to a member's record was accepted or refused, with the reason code that says which, on its way back to the proposer. The boundary carries the verdict and forms none of its own. Derived from the emits list of member@1.6.0

a refusal from one of a member's holders -- a screened-off turn, or a question the memory would not take. It must leave the namespace for the same reason it must leave the member: a level that consumed it would be a holder, and a silently swallowed refusal is exactly what GH #284 took out of this tree. Undrained above, it becomes no_route in the DLQ, which is recorded and self-localising. Derived from the emits list of member@1.6.0

a member failed at something that was not a refusal; which holder, channel or assistant inside produced it is not the caller's business and even less the namespace's. The boundary is not a consumer: an error that crosses a namespace is one the parent owes a drain. Derived from the emits list of member@1.6.0

an assistant's batched conversation write, on its way out through the namespace. The boundary neither reads it nor keeps a copy -- what a member's assistant said belongs to that member (GH #122, the three-holders ruling), and an org that stored it would be a holder rather than a namespace. Derived from the emits list of member@1.6.0

one finished turn a member's assistant offers for archiving, one message per turn, crossing the namespace untouched. Same reason as `write`: a group is an audience, not a holder, so the boundary carries the turn and never files it. Since GH #527 the member no longer only passes it on -- it fans a copy onto its OWN memory hive's `in_episode`, the one path from a conversation into an `episodes` table -- and this lane is unchanged by that: what arrives here is the copy that left the member, and it is still the parent's to place or to drain. Derived from the emits list of member@1.6.0

a housekeeping report from a member's assistant, raised when something above fired the prune lane. The namespace owns no timer and no schedule; it is a boundary, and it lets the report out instead of swallowing it. Derived from the emits list of member@1.6.0

a structural wish or a submission leaving one of this organisation's members, on its way to the one baumeister the whole colony shares. Declared here because it CROSSES this level and no sibling inside it consumes it (ADR-0013), and for no other reason: this level stays a namespace and a boundary, not a participant -- no cell is added and the container stays empty. Derived from the emits list of member@1.6.0

the receipt of a close pass: what the strong model added, sharpened, corrected, closed or restated when it read one ended session whole. It leaves the namespace because a member does not read its own receipt and an org is not a holder -- the boundary carries it and files nothing. Derived from the emits list of member@1.6.0

a member's memory has been written out completely, marker file and all. Same reason as every other lane here: the namespace neither triggers the export nor keeps what it produced, and the level that asked for it is somewhere above this boundary. Derived from the emits list of member@1.6.0

the receipt of one applied import part, on its way out through the namespace. Same reason as every other member receipt this level carries: the org reads nothing in it and decides nothing about it. Derived from the emits list of member@1.6.0 (GH #555)

the receipt of one identity pack, on its way out of the level (GH #458). Nothing in here consumes it and nothing in here can: the record that pushed the identity keeps its own delivery stamp, and a receipt is evidence for whoever operates the colony. TWO travel per pack, one per occupant of the generation it reached. Derived from the emits list of member@1.6.0 -- a level that did not declare it would let a real, recurring message die as no_route at its own boundary

description.purpose: Scope marker of an organisation: a name, a boundary, and one open container its members are instantiated into. It carries no cell of any kind -- an org that grows a cell has stopped being a namespace. Its twenty edges are the whole of its behaviour: eight doors down into ./members and twelve exits back out, one per lane of the contract.
description.use_when: One per organisation, instantiated into the shell's orgs container. Instantiate it in the mutation that also wires its transit lanes, one edge each; the hive is an island until an edge crosses into it. Members are instantiated into ./members afterwards, one at a time, and each of those mutations draws its own edges.
description.not_in_scope: No memory: a group is an audience, not a holder, and 'what does the group know about X' is a filter on the read, never a second store (GH #122). No identity, no broker, no firewall, no drain, no sink -- every one of those is either a member's own or the shell's. No cells at all, and no routing below ./members: until a member is instantiated there is nothing down there to route to.
description.contract_derivation: The lanes are the union of what member@1.6.0 accepts and emits, minus the lanes a sibling inside this level consumes itself. Nothing is subtracted: the only thing inside an org is the container, so there is no sibling to consume anything. Note in particular that 'turn' is NOT here -- a member consumes its own turn internally (./channels -> ./firewall since GH #454, ./assistants -> ./firewall before it) and never emits one. The last three emits -- write, turn_write, prune -- are what a member re-emits on behalf of its assistants and nothing at member level consumes; they arrived here when the member started carrying them, because the derivation is read off the neighbour's file rather than kept by hand. Two more arrived with R6 (GH #425): `build` upward and `in_build_result` downward, the lane pair that carries an agentically initiated structural wish to the one baumeister the colony shares and the answer back. They are transit in the purest form this level has -- the org reads nothing in either, adds no cell for them, and its container stays empty. Thinness is the property under test (ADR-0013 corollary b), and two lanes plus two edges through an empty container is exactly what this level already does for in_turn/answer. Three more arrived with GH #447: `in_export` downward and `close_report` + `export_done` upward. The first two are the close pass and its receipt -- the member fires the pass on its own closed sessions, so nothing about it enters here, but the receipt has to leave; the third is the completion word of a memory export whose parts never cross this level at all, because they land on disk inside the member. Transit again, and again with no cell: three lanes, three edges, an empty container. Two more arrived after that: `pack_ack` with GH #458 -- the receipt of an identity pack a member's own record pushed into one of its generations, which nothing in here consumes and nothing in here can -- and `in_import` with GH #467, the return leg of `in_export`, one part of a memory document on its way into the hive of the member it belongs to. Both are transit with no cell, exactly like the rest. GH #454 moved no lane across this boundary and that is the finding rather than a non-event: the channels went from the assistant to the member, so the assistant's `turn` stopped existing and its `answer` started crossing -- and the member absorbed both, consuming the answer at its own ./channels and carrying only the unaddressed remainder out on a lane this level already declared. A level that is a namespace is exactly the level a rearrangement one storey down does not reach. One more arrived with GH #533: `bundle`. `in_recall` has crossed this level since it was written and its answer had nowhere to go -- `bundle` was in nobody's emits list, at any of the three levels an outside recall has to leave, so the answer died inside the member's assistants container. The lane is transit like every other here: the org reads neither the bundle nor the reply-to token that addresses it, and adds no cell for either.
